record.paper_title: Some open questions in axion theory
record.original_question: If one solves the problem of fermion effects in the axion-dyon system, does electromagnetism by itself imply a nonzero lower bound on the mass of an axion coupled to our photon, even in the absence of non-Abelian instantons?

evidence.quote: Solving this could address related interesting phenomenological questions such as whether there exists a minimum mass of the axion coupling to our electromagnetism, even without non-Abelian instantons.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a four-dimensional U(1) gauge theory (electromagnetism) coupled to a pseudoscalar field a (the axion) through the standard topological interaction

  L ⊃ (1/2)(∂a)^2 − (a/(8π^2 f_a)) F ∧ F,

where f_a is the axion decay constant and F is the U(1) field strength. Assume the gauge theory admits magnetic monopoles and dyons (so that the full spectrum realizes electric–magnetic duality), and that all relevant charged fermion sectors coupled to the photon and to the axion-dyon system are properly incorporated (including any anomaly inflow and fermion zero-mode effects on dyon states).

Assume there are no non-Abelian gauge sectors and hence no contributions to the axion potential from non-Abelian instantons.

Question: Does the U(1) gauge dynamics together with its monopole/dyon spectrum and the associated fermion effects necessarily generate a nontrivial potential for a, so that the axion mass m_a is bounded below by a strictly positive constant m_a ≥ m_min > 0 determined by electromagnetic data alone? Equivalently, prove or disprove that electromagnetism by itself forces a nonzero lower bound on the mass of an axion coupled to the photon.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether the axion-monopole/dyon system generates a nontrivial axion potential—and hence a minimum axion mass from electromagnetism alone—remains an active research question. Recent work on axion-monopole couplings, the Witten effect on axions, and fermion zero modes on dyons (e.g., Fan–Fraser–Reece–Stout 2021, Csaki et al. 2023, Brennan 2023) has discussed but not definitively resolved whether a strictly positive lower bound on m_a is implied without non-Abelian instantons.

status_evidence.title: Axion mass from magnetic monopole loops
status_evidence.snippet: Fan, Fraser, Reece, Stout discuss whether monopoles generate an axion potential; the issue of fermion zero modes on dyons is highlighted as unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: The contribution of dyons (with fermion zero modes) to the axion potential is not settled, leaving the existence of an electromagnetic lower bound on m_a open.

status_evidence.title: Some open questions in axion theory
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the existence of a minimum axion mass from electromagnetism, even without non-Abelian instantons, as an open phenomenological question.
status_evidence.claim: The question is identified as open.
